title: Sort Employees by Hire Date
description:
Retrieve all employees ordered from the **earliest hire date** to the most recent.

**Table: employees** — `id`, `name`, `department`, `hire_date`

Return `id`, `name`, and `hire_date`. Order by `hire_date` ascending.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, department VARCHAR, hire_date DATE); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Alice','Engineering','2021-03-15'),(2,'Bob','Sales','2019-07-22'),(3,'Carol','HR','2022-11-01'),(4,'Dave','Engineering','2018-04-10'),(5,'Eve','Marketing','2023-06-30'),(6,'Frank','Sales','2020-01-15'),(7,'Grace','Engineering','2024-02-28');
solution_sql: SELECT id, name, hire_date FROM employees ORDER BY hire_date ASC

test_cases.description: All 7 employees returned, ordered from earliest hire date (Dave 2018) to latest (Grace 2024)

hints: ORDER BY hire_date ASC sorts from oldest to newest. ASC is the default so it can be omitted.
Date columns sort correctly when stored as DATE type — no casting needed.
explanation: ORDER BY hire_date ASC sorts rows in ascending chronological order. The correct order is: Dave (2018-04-10), Bob (2019-07-22), Frank (2020-01-15), Alice (2021-03-15), Carol (2022-11-01), Eve (2023-06-30), Grace (2024-02-28).
